title: Opinions: creer que and no creer que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *creo que* + indicative and *no creo que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 7; the same rule works for *creen que* and *no creen que*. They are the natural tools for a debate among historians: say whose opinion it is, then use the right mood.

sections.title: Mood after creer
rows: Algunos historiadores creen que conquista es la palabra correcta.
Otros no creen que esta palabra explique todo.
Muchos historiadores creen que las enfermedades mataron a muchas personas.

items.spanish: Algunos historiadores creen que conquista es la palabra correcta.
items.english: Some historians believe that conquest is the right word.

items.spanish: Otros no creen que esta palabra explique todo.
items.english: Others do not believe that this word explains everything.

items.spanish: Muchos historiadores creen que las enfermedades mataron a muchas personas.
items.english: Many historians believe that diseases killed many people.

items.spanish: Algunos historiadores no creen que la leyenda negra sea falsa por completo.
items.english: Some historians do not believe that the black legend is completely false.

sections.content: In a debate about the past, always attribute the opinion (*algunos historiadores creen que…*, *otros no creen que…*) instead of giving your own. *Creer que* accepts the idea (indicative); *no creer que* doubts it (subjunctive).
